Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. Our security team has a couple of follow-ups before we kick off the POC. Can you confirm in plain terms: where user input and model inference are executed (regions), which subprocessors may touch payloads, and how deletion/retention works end-to-end?

Specifically:
- If our EU users hit your hosted API, can we ensure inference never leaves EU physical hosts?
- Which cloud providers or partners (subprocessors) are in the request/response path?
- How long is request data retained in logs/KV caches and what is the deletion SLA after a deletion request?

Appreciate short bullet answers and any artifacts you can share (map, timeline).

Best,

Elena — thanks for the clear list. High level answers up front, then I attach a short map and timeline. Happy to run through this live if helpful.

High level (short bullets):
- Regional execution: Hosted API routes by customer region. For EU customers we route to EU-hosted clusters by default (Frankfurt, Amsterdam). For US customers we use US clusters (us-east-1, us-west-2). We also offer Private (VPC) deployments if you need fully customer-managed hosts.
- Subprocessors: Primary cloud providers (AWS, GCP) operate the compute. We also use a managed cache layer (EvCache Inc.) and an observability vendor (TraceSight) that receives anonymized metrics only. Subprocessors list and contract links are in the attached map.
- Retention and deletion: Request payloads are transient by default — tokenization and KV cache entries are ephemeral. Logs required for billing/ops are retained 30 days by default; customers can request 0- or 7-day retention on enterprise plans. Deletion SLA: tombstone applied within 24 hours; complete removal from backups within 30 days (we provide a signed attestation).

Attachments included: data_processing_map.pdf (processing sites & subprocessors), residency_matrix.csv (configurable retention by plan), SOC2_attestation_redacted.pdf (control summary).

If Novamed needs EU-only physical residency for the inference plane, we can:
- Pin the project to EU-hosted clusters (no egress to US),
- Disable cross-region failover for the POC, and
- Provide an audit token-level log extract on request.

Next step: Are you able to share whether the requirement is "EU execution only" or broader (e.g., "data must not cross to non-EEA subprocessors")? That tells us whether Private deployment is required.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni

Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where my data actually runs and how it's deleted

Samir — answering each point below, keeping to the facts you can include in security review docs.

1) TraceSight: we send only aggregated telemetry (token counts, latency histograms, error codes). No full request/response payloads, no user identifiers. PII fields are redacted at the edge before metrics emission. You can request a telemetry sample schema (we attached the schema to the drive link).

2) EvCache (managed cache): for hosted POCs we can provision a regional EvCache cluster in the EU that persists only within the region. By default caches are regional and not replicated across continents unless explicitly enabled. For your POC we'll pin caches to eu-central-1.

3) KV cache and tombstone behavior: when a deletion/tombstone request is issued we:
  - mark the key as deleted in the control plane immediately (within seconds),
  - issue an eviction and CTX purge to the cache nodes (propagates within minutes),
  - prevent rehydration by blacklisting the associated model session tokens for 24 hours, and
  - run a background sweep to zero out in-memory KV on the nodes; any snapshots/backups are shredded per backup retention (30 days by default).

We will also provide a short attestation of these steps for your legal team. If you require faster backup shredding windows we can discuss an enterprise SLA.

Action items:
- I'll share a short 1-page technical attestation and the EvCache regional provisioning excerpt (attached).
- Vivek: confirm whether Novamed wants regional-only hosted POC or to move to a private VPC.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Security, Redwood Inference
